title: Windows GPU unit tests job fails extracting OpenVINO packages due to locked tbb12.dll
signature: windows runner extract openvino packages expand-archive remove-item access to the path denied unauthorizedaccessexception locked dll file|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails: Remove-Item cannot overwrite tbb12.dll, Access to the path is denied (UnauthorizedAccessException).

key_errors:
Remove-Item : Cannot remove item C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll:
Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
At C:\Windows\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive\Microsoft.PowerShell.Archive.psm1:1029
+ CategoryInfo          : PermissionDenied: (C:\actions-runn...b\bin\tbb12.dll:FileInfo) [Remove-Item], UnauthorizedAccessException
+ FullyQualifiedErrorId : RemoveFileSystemItemUnAuthorizedAccess,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.RemoveItemCommand
root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs Expand-Archive -Force against a pre-existing install directory on the self-hosted Windows runner. Expand-Archive with -Force tries to delete existing files before overwriting them, but tbb12.dll from a prior job/process on the same stateful runner is still locked (likely held open by an antivirus scanner, a lingering OpenVINO process, or a DLL still mapped by a previous test run that was not fully terminated/cleaned up). This is a recurring Windows self-hosted runner workspace-cleanliness/stale-handle issue, not a code defect; it has recurred 10+ times historically under the same pattern signature and is unrelated to the PR's GPU clang-tidy changes.
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires a Windows self-hosted runner workspace where a previous job left tbb12.dll locked. Can be approximated locally on Windows by holding tbb12.dll open (e.g., loading it into a running process) and then re-running Expand-Archive -Force over the same install directory.
recommended_actions: Add a workspace-cleanup/reset step before 'Extract OpenVINO packages' that forcibly closes lingering OpenVINO-related processes (e.g., taskkill on test binaries) prior to archive extraction.

Replace blanket Expand-Archive -Force with a pre-clean step that removes the previous install/runtime directory with retry/backoff logic (e.g., loop with Start-Sleep and repeated Remove-Item attempts) before extracting.
Investigate whether an antivirus/indexing service on the runner is holding a handle on tbb12.dll immediately after artifact download, and exclude the workspace path from real-time AV scanning.
Consider using ephemeral/clean Windows runners for this job to avoid stale file locks carried over between jobs.
prevention_strategies: Ensure Windows self-hosted runners fully terminate all spawned processes and release file handles at the end of each job (job cleanup hook). Add a pre-step that waits/retries on Remove-Item failures with exponential backoff instead of failing immediately. Track this known-flaky infrastructure pattern and consider runner pool health alerts if occurrence count grows further.
historical_context: This exact signature (514ffa2ab52ad344) has now recurred 12 times since 2026-11-09, making it the most frequent known pattern in the post-commit database. Related but distinct patterns include a missing onednn license file variant (33e8544b41961fd6, 1 occurrence) and a PowerShell execution-policy variant (3be0e72d6ae29098, 4 occurrences) in the same 'Extract OpenVINO packages' / GPU unit tests job.
